title: BizFlood Policy Services Reference — Renewal Offer Timing, Notice Periods and Signed Requests
content:
Each tier of BizFlood Commercial Flood Policies (Surplus Lines) fixes how many days before term end the renewal offer is issued, whether a signed statement of values is required to renew, the written notice before term end for a Tidemark non-renewal, the written notice before Tidemark cancels for nonpayment or misrepresentation, and whether requests must be signed by an authorized signer of the insured entity.

## Reference table

| Tier | Renewal offer issued before term end (calendar days) | Signed statement of values required to renew | Non-renewal notice before term end (calendar days) | Notice before an insurer cancellation (calendar days) | Requests signed by an authorized signer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BizFlood Building | 60 | Yes | 60 | 30 | Required |
| BizFlood Building and Contents | 60 | Yes | 60 | 30 | Required |
| BizFlood Building, Contents and Business Income | 60 | Yes | 60 | 30 | Required |
| BizFlood Excess over NFIP | 60 | Yes | 60 | 30 | Required |
| BizFlood Multi-Location | 60 | Yes | 60 | 30 | Required |
| BizFlood Large Property | 60 | Yes | 90 | 30 | Required |

## Points of reading

- BizFlood Large Property is the only tier with a longer non-renewal notice: 90 calendar days instead of 60.
- On every tier a signed statement of values is required to renew, and every request must be signed by an authorized signer of the insured entity.
- The notice before Tidemark cancels for nonpayment or misrepresentation is 30 calendar days on every tier.

## Counting illustration (hypothetical dates)

For a hypothetical term ending on 30 June, a 60-day offer period is counted back 60 calendar days from that term end, to 1 May; a 90-day non-renewal notice on BizFlood Large Property is counted back 90 calendar days, to 1 April.
